title: SDK Prospect Lab: Quickrun Cookbook
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight, repeatable lab cookbook that Solutions/SEs and Developer-advocates can run with a prospect in a 20–40 minute session. Goal: get a real request/response going, demonstrate performance/latency characteristics, show cost & observability signals, and leave the prospect with an artifact (tiny sample app + trace).

Why a separate "prospect lab"?
- Prospect sessions need to be frictionless and fast. Not the full onboarding playbook; this is about proof-of-value in front of technical buyers.
- Emphasize measurable outcomes: token latency, tokens/second, one-minute cost estimate, simple SLA behaviour (retry/circuit).
- Include sales-friendly checkpoints (success criteria) so SEs know when to pivot to next conversation.

Audience / Personas
- Platform engineer evaluating inference runtime for product features
- ML engineer doing a prototype integration to assess latency and cost
- Technical product manager who wants to see an end-to-end demo quickly

Pre-session checklist (10–15 min prep)
- Confirm prospect has a public repo or small code sample to adapt (ideal). If not, we use the sample-app template.
- Provision a short-lived API key (time-limited) or use the demo account sandbox.
- Pre-select model variant to demo (recommend: gpt2-ish tiny open model for token-speed demo + a larger verified model for quality).
- Create a workspace in Console for the session with telemetry turned on (trace retention default).
- Prepare 3 short prompts tailored to the prospect's domain (customer-support example, search re-ranking, code summary).

Session structure (20–40 minutes)
1) 3 min — Quick context and outcome goals
   - Say: "By the end you'll have a runnable example, seen latency/cost, and observed one regression test run."
2) 7–12 min — Hands-on run: sample app + SDK call
   - Clone tiny-sample-app (polyglot template). Walk through 3 files: README, run-locally script, sdk-call snippet.
   - Run locally with our SDK in node/python. Show streaming response vs non-streaming.
   - Command pattern: `curl` quicktest -> SDK call -> trace link in console.
3) 5–8 min — Probe: latency and throughput checks
   - Use built-in microbench: 10 sequential requests for p50/p95, then 8 concurrent (small concurrency) to show queueing and autoscale behaviour.
   - Record numbers in the ephemeral lab note: p50, p95, mean tokens/sec, avg token cost estimate.
4) 3–7 min — Observability & cost demo
   - Open Console: show per-request token breakdown, operation trace, tail-latency spike if present, cost estimate widget.
   - Show an example of automatic fallback (policy) if a model variant is offline.
5) 2–5 min — Next steps and artifact handoff
   - Deliver the repo link, trace links, and a 3-line follow-up note with recommended next steps.

Runbook details / commands (shorthand)
- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/demo-prospect-lab (starter)
- Quick local run (python):
  - `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate`
  - `pip install -r requirements.txt`
  - `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=demo_xxx`
  - `python run_prompt.py "Summarize customer ticket: ..." --stream`
- Node quick test: `node quick-run.mjs` (uses streaming client)
- Microbench: `./microbench --model small-v1 --seq 256 --concurrency 8 --count 10` (returns p50/p95/tokens/s)

Kit pieces included in the repo
- tiny-sample-app (JS + Python) scaffold
- microbench script (shell + tiny node utility)
- console-link generator: `make-trace-link <trace-id>`
- example llm prompt set (3 prompts) per domain (support, docs, code)

Checklist for SE during run
- Confirm API key is scoped and will expire (security comfort)
- Run non-stream and stream; call out UX differences
- Run a payload with long context (prefix caching demo) to show KV cache benefits
- Trigger a fallback scenario (simulate a model timeout) to show fallback routing
- Note the trace URL and capture the request/response ids to attach to the follow-up

Observability talking points (what to call out)
- Token-level latencies and breakdown (tokenization, kernel, queue)
- Cost per request: tokens * model unit cost — show quick math and extrapolate to typical traffic pattern (e.g., 1k/day -> monthly cost)
- Telemetry: sampling rate, logs, error rates, tagging by customer route
- Traces: span breakdowns for SDK call -> routing -> runtime execution -> response streaming

Quality/Regression quick demo
- Use the prompt-eval harness in repo to run a tiny eval (3 prompts) against baseline model and a candidate variant. Show pass/fail and a simple diff of outputs.
- Explain how Redwood Optimize suggestions could be used after pilot to tune quantization and batching for cost/quality tradeoff.

Failure modes to show (brief)
- 429 bursts: show how rate limiting manifests in SDK and what circuit breaker behavior we recommend
- Tokenization surprises: large tokens causing longer kernel runtimes — demonstrate with a payload
- Network flakiness: fake a dropped packet and surface how retries & idempotency work in the SDK

Handoff artifact (what we deliver to prospect)
- Fork of tiny-sample-app with configured demo API key (time-limited) + README tailored to them
- Lab notes (one-page) with p50/p95 tokens/sec, cost estimate, and suggested next three steps
- Trace links for representative requests

Success criteria for conversion to POC
- SE/ML says prototype can be integrated in <2 weeks with existing infra
- Observed p95 latency under target (customer-specific) for the sample workload
- Cost estimate within prospect's expected budget band
- Prospect agrees to a short technical POC scope (list of endpoints, data requirements)

Open questions / TODOs
- Add an automated "export lab report" feature to the repo that compiles p50/p95 and cost estimates as a PDF (nice to have).
- Validate the microbench parameters across GPUs (A10 vs A100); current defaults are tuned on A10s.
- Need a shorter one-command demo for non-technical POCs (button in Console to "Run demo and share report").
- Security: confirm legal about issuing time-limited demo keys to prospects (Sofia to follow up).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the lab under 40 minutes. Best conversions happen if we finish within 30.
- Emphasize two things: measurable performance and a tangible artifact.
- Avoid deep dives into rollout policies unless the prospect asks (can derail timebox).

References and links
- Canvas: CONFLUENCE-ENG-SDK-ONBOARD-2025 (detailed onboarding)
- Example PR for tiny-sample-app: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/412
- Linear ticket for lab automation: linear/SDKS-98
